findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 evidence cites the 'sanity-bound' case at packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:442-448 as proof that the retained sanity bound 'is exercised rather than silently absent,' but that case only asserts TRANSCRIPT.length > 200_000 and that the digest matches /^story_advance\/[0-9a-f]{12}$/ -- a well-formed-digest check that passes identically whether or not the .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) bound exists in convergence-breaker.ts:483-485. Verified empirically: removed the .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) call from convergence-breaker.ts, rebuilt, and ran this exact assertion pair in isolation against the bound-removed build -- it still PASSED. The bound-removed build IS caught, but by a different case: 'must-still-collapse beyond-sanity-bound' (smoke.ts:337-341, MUST_COLLAPSE lane), which is the evidence cited for the separate intent CHK-001:edge:1, not for edge:0. So CHK-001:edge:0 has no valid evidence of its own claimed property; that property is established elsewhere under a different intentRef. This is an evidence note that restates the intent rather than an assertion that proves it. Net risk is low (the bound is genuinely tested by edge:1), but the edge:0 evidence record itself does not cover what it claims.
findings.resolvedReason: Replaced the tautological sanity-bound assertion. MAX_REASON_CHARS is now exported from convergence-breaker.ts and the smoke asserts gateFailureDigest(cmd, TRANSCRIPT) === gateFailureDigest(cmd, TRANSCRIPT.slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS)) as matrix case 'sanity-bound-is-applied'. Revert-proof against the built dist: deleting .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) fails exactly sanity-bound/sanity-bound-is-applied and sanity-bound/beyond-sanity-bound, 18 other cases still passing — the old well-formed-digest check passed under that same deletion. The no-throw shape check is retained but explicitly labelled a shape check, not evidence the bound exists.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the narrowed digit-rule regex `(?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-])` only treats a digit run as identifier-attached when preceded/followed by a word char or ASCII hyphen; a `.` does not protect. Verified empirically: normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.229 or newer") and normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.230 or newer") both reduce to "requires lattice-cli v0.#.# or newer" (identical digest). Any rejection reason embedding a dotted version/semver string (a realistic shape given version-bump.ts already formats messages like "expected X.Y.Z") collapses two substantively different failures into one gate-failure key -- exactly the C4 over-collapse class this story exists to fix, for a token shape CHK-003/CHK-004 never exercises. gateFailureDigest is exported general-purpose, not scoped to the one current call site.
findings.resolvedReason: The number rule's protection set was widened from [\w-] to [\w.-], so a digit run attached by a dot is treated as part of the identifier: 'requires lattice-cli v0.3.229 or newer' and the same message with v0.3.230 now keep separate digest keys. Guarded by must-differ case 'dotted-version-requirement' (guard: digit-rule), which drives the real counter and asserts keys=2 counter=1. Revert-proof: restoring the round-1 form (?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-]) fails digit-rule/dotted-version-requirement and digit-rule/negative-counter with the other 18 passing.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the digit-rule lookbehind/lookahead `(?<![\w-])...(?![\w-])` excludes a preceding/following ASCII hyphen unconditionally, which also matches a minus sign, so a negative number is treated as identifier-attached and survives instead of collapsing. Verified: normalize("retry budget -5 remaining") vs normalize("retry budget -19 remaining") do NOT collapse (stay distinct), unlike the documented free-standing-counter behavior in the surrounding comment (attempt 41, 3>=2, 0/4 lanes all correctly collapse). This under-collapses an incidental numeric difference, i.e. it is a live instance of the exact risk plan.md #4 calls out as the change's central danger ("the change makes the breaker fire less often ... a stuck agent [could] regain an unbounded retry loop"), for a token shape (negative numbers) the CHK-004 must-still-collapse lane never tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Re-decided in round 4 and recorded as superseded rather than silently reverted. This finding asked the digest to collapse -5 and -19 by treating a leading minus as a sign rather than an identifier hyphen. Honouring it requires the general free-standing-number rule, and that rule is exactly what collapsed the F-020 shapes — it cannot distinguish retry budget -5 from got -0.61 in real test output. No producer in this tree emits a bare countdown into a gate rejection, so the finding asked the digest to collapse an ambiguous bare number with nothing on the volatile side of the scale. The fixture is NOT deleted: it is converted to must-differ case negative-counter-now-distinct, tagged number-rule-removal, so the change of decision is visible in the matrix output. Rationale and residual recorded in plan.md section 4.2 and 4.3.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:463-468 — the function's top JSDoc still states the error message is "normalized to strip volatile tokens (hashes, ids, timestamps, bare numbers, paths)" unqualified. This is now inaccurate: CHK-002 narrowed path-stripping to token-start absolute paths only (relative repo paths and mid-token slashes like DEV/REVIEW are deliberately left untouched), and CHK-003 narrowed number-stripping to standalone numbers only (identifier-attached digits like CHK-001 are deliberately preserved). A maintainer reading only this doc comment would believe ALL paths and ALL bare numbers are still stripped, which is precisely the kind of doc/implementation mismatch this story's own root cause (an over-broad implementation vs. a narrower intended contract) illustrates. The doc comment should name the narrower rule (token-start absolute paths; standalone digit runs) so a future edit does not re-widen the regex believing it is restoring documented behavior.
findings.resolvedReason: The gateFailureDigest JSDoc was rewritten from the unqualified 'bare numbers, paths' claim to a per-rule description of what the normalizer actually does: hex/0x/ISO tokens; absolute paths ONLY at a token start (POSIX and Windows) with relative repo paths and mid-token slashes explicitly named as deliberately untouched; durations/sizes with a unit suffix; and standalone numbers only, with identifier-attached digits (CHK-001, B-bf52, round-2, v0.3.229) explicitly named as deliberately preserved. It also states that widening re-introduces the false freeze and that narrowing the duration/number rule re-introduces the livelock, and points at the smoke as the case-by-case guard. The retained sanity bound got its own exported doc comment.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:316-318 — the new must-still-collapse case 'timestamp-and-attempt-counter' uses the exact same two literal fixture strings ("gate BLOCKED for B-bbaf at 2026-07-14T00:00:00Z (attempt 3)" / "...T09:59:59Z (attempt 41)") already asserted for digest-equality and counter-accumulation-to-2 at lines 165-166 and 172-173 in the pre-existing section 7 (unchanged by this diff). The new section 7b matrix explicitly frames itself (comment at line ~182) as replacing the removed ALPHA/BETA fixture and adding fresh must-differ/must-still-collapse coverage, but this one case adds no new coverage over the pre-existing K1 timestamp/attempt-counter assertion it duplicates -- same input strings, same digest-equality check, same counter-reaches-2 check, run twice under two different code paths for no additional signal.
findings.resolvedReason: The duplicated 'timestamp-and-attempt-counter' matrix case (identical fixture strings to the pre-existing section-7 assertion at smoke.ts:165-174) was removed. The pre-existing section-7 assertion still covers ISO timestamps plus a free-standing attempt counter. In its place the collapse lane gained genuinely new coverage: the four real lease/lock heartbeat-age messages, negative counters, delimiter-attached and Windows absolute paths, and the applied sanity bound — 12 collapse cases in total, none duplicating another.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:502 — the path-rule regex `(?:^|(?<=[\s"'(\[]))\/[^\s"')\]]*` only recognizes POSIX-style absolute paths (leading `/`). A Windows-style absolute path such as `C:\Users\jek\file1.ts` vs `C:\Users\other\file2.ts` is left completely untouched by every normalization rule (no leading slash, and digits inside `file1`/`file2` are word-attached so the digit-rule also leaves them alone) and so the two machine-specific paths do NOT collapse to one digest -- verified empirically. The design comment at :500-501 explicitly claims the rule "behaves identically on macOS and Linux" (i.e. Windows was consciously out of scope), so this may be an accepted gap rather than an oversight, but it reproduces the same host-varying-path-does-not-collapse failure mode this story exists to fix if this CLI is ever run from a Windows host.
findings.resolvedReason: Windows absolute paths are now normalized by a dedicated rule (?:^|(?<=[\s"'(\[:=,]))[a-z]:\\[^\s"')\]]* applied before the POSIX rule, and the token-start delimiter set of both path rules was widened to include : = and , so a path introduced without a separating space (cwd=/Users/...) also collapses. Guarded by must-still-collapse cases 'windows-absolute-path' (guard: windows-path-rule) and 'delimiter-attached-absolute-path' (guard: path-rule). Revert-proof: deleting the Windows rule fails exactly windows-path-rule/windows-absolute-path with the other 19 passing.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 the narrowed standalone-number rule `(?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-])` does not normalize a digit run directly attached to a UNIT-LETTER suffix (e.g. 45s, 5m, 2h) because the follow-char is a word character, so the negative lookahead blocks the match. Three real, story_advance-reachable rejection messages embed exactly this shape via formatLeaseAge/formatLockAge (heartbeat `${age} ago`, age like 45s/5m/2h): (1) packages/main/src/core/story-owner-lease.ts:591-598,616-640 formatLeaseAge/formatNonOwnerError (thrown from cli/ownership-gate.ts non-owner story_advance rejection -- the common no-lease-owned-by-me path), (2) packages/main/src/cli/ownership-gate.ts:301-306 active-lease --takeover rejection, (3) packages/main/src/core/main-write-lock.ts:71-113 formatLockAge/buildMainWriteLockContentionMessage (DONE-phase main-write-lock contention), (4) packages/main/src/core/validation-execution-lock.ts:233-262 formatLockAge/buildValidationLockContentionMessage (TEST-phase validation-lock contention). Verified against the built packages/main/dist/core/convergence-breaker.js: gateFailureDigest(story_advance, msg-with-45s) !== gateFailureDigest(story_advance, msg-with-46s) for all four message shapes (confirmed by direct node execution), so a story_advance retried against an actively-heartbeating foreign lease or a held lock gets a NEW digest key on essentially every retry and maxGateFailureCount never reaches 2 -- assessBreaker never trips gate-repeat for exactly the runaway-retry-loop scenario the breaker exists to catch. Confirmed this is a functional REGRESSION: the OLD unconditional /\d+/g rule DID collapse these same two messages to one key (verified directly), so narrowing broke a previously-working case. This also falsifies the CHK-003 verificationIntent edge claim recorded in plan.md #3 (Confirmed no production rejection message embeds a volatile counter attached to an identifier: the only attached-counter shapes in the tree are step record ids at planned-steps-executor.ts:1298 and :1309, and that module throws no Error) -- that module indeed throws nothing, but the heartbeat-age shape above DOES throw reachable Errors and was missed by that survey. None of CHK-004s must-still-collapse matrix cases (packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts) exercise a digit-attached-to-unit-letter shape -- its only counter/timestamp case uses ISO-8601 timestamps plus a free-standing (attempt N) counter -- so the regression guard does not catch this. Fix: normalize the digit+unit-letter age shape (e.g. \\b\\d+[smh]\\b) before/alongside the standalone-number rule, or normalize via the formatted age helper output generally.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed as a functional regression and fixed with a duration/size rule (?<![\w.-])-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:ms|s|m|h|d|kb|mb|gb|b)(?![\w.-]) applied immediately before the number rule, so a digit run welded to a unit letter is consumed together with its unit. All four story_advance-reachable sources named in the finding are now must-still-collapse fixtures reproduced from their build sites — story-owner-lease.ts:616-640 (formatNonOwnerError), cli/ownership-gate.ts:301-306 (active-lease --takeover refusal), main-write-lock.ts:96-118 and validation-execution-lock.ts:243-262 — each varying only the heartbeat age (and the holder pid where present), each asserting keys=1 counter=2 and that assessBreaker trips with gate-repeat 2>=2. Revert-proof: deleting the duration rule fails exactly those four cases (duration-rule/lease-non-owner-heartbeat-age, active-lease-takeover-refusal, main-write-lock-contention, validation-lock-contention) and leaves the other 16 passing. plan.md section 3 was rewritten to retract the false survey claim this finding disproved, name the four sources and record the duration rule as the answer.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts userSees text for CHK-002 and CHK-003 (and to a lesser extent CHK-001) describes prose that a human reading the console output would supposedly see (e.g. CHK-002 userSees: the smoke prints passing checks stating that DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently...and that the same lock path under /Users and under /private/var still digests identically; CHK-003 userSees: a passing check stating that a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently). I ran node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js and the actual printed lines for these cases are terse machine-readable tags with no literal mention of the compared values, e.g. `  must-differ         phase-pair [guard: path-rule] keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed` and `  must-differ         checklist-ordinal [guard: digit-rule] keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed` and `  must-still-collapse machine-absolute-path [guard: collapse-lane] keys=1 counter=2 breaker=trips`. The literal strings DEV/REVIEW, DEV/TEST, /Users, /private/var, CHK-001, CHK-002 never appear anywhere in the printed output -- only abstract case-name tags (phase-pair, machine-absolute-path, checklist-ordinal) do, and a reader would have to open the source file to learn which literal values each tag represents. The functional claim (keys differ / collapse, counter value) IS correctly proven, but the userSees text overstates what the printed output literally states, describing prose sentences that do not appear on screen. CHK-004s userSees ("lists the must-differ and must-still-collapse digest cases by name, each reporting the resulting gate-failure counter value") is accurate and matches the real output. Suggest tightening CHK-001/002/003 userSees to describe the actual tag+keys/counter/breaker format rather than implying literal value names are printed.
findings.resolvedReason: userSees is frozen, so the OUTPUT was changed to match the promise instead. Every matrix case now prints its two literal compared reason values under its tag, plus the verdict in words ('the two values DIGEST DIFFERENTLY' / 'DIGEST IDENTICALLY') and the index of the first character at which the pair diverges. DEV/REVIEW vs DEV/TEST, /Users vs /private/var, CHK-001 vs CHK-002 and src/core/alpha.ts vs src/core/beta.ts now appear literally on screen. Values longer than 150 chars print a window centred on the first differing character rather than a head-truncated prefix, because the DEV-gate pair is byte-identical for its first 617 characters — a head preview would have printed two identical strings and shown nothing, and the printed divergence index is itself the CHK-001 evidence that the difference lies past the former 200-character cut.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B) finding, recorded by the main agent because codex-cli is not a registered dispatch actor: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts — MAX_REASON_CHARS slices the RAW reason as UTF-16 code units before normalization, so a reason of the form 'x'.repeat(16383) + an astral character leaves a lone high surrogate (0xd83d) as the final unit, which hashes as replacement encoding rather than the original character. Deterministic, so no cross-call instability, but the bound is not Unicode code-point safe. Fix: drop a trailing lone high surrogate after the slice.
findings.resolvedReason: The sanity bound is now applied by boundReasonForDigest(), which slices to MAX_REASON_CHARS and then drops a trailing lone high surrogate (charCode in 0xd800-0xdbff), so the bound can no longer leave half of an astral character to be hashed as a replacement encoding. Evidence strength recorded as medium: the surrogate trim itself is covered by inspection and the direction check rather than by a dedicated smoke fixture, since the observable consequence is a digest-input difference and not a behavioural divergence. The same finding's path-delimiter half is fixed and guarded as described under F-006.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:161-198 (section 7, unchanged by the F-008 fix) — CHK-003 userSees promises the smoke prints "a passing check stating that a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently, ALONGSIDE a passing check that two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still digest identically." The F-008 fix added literal-value printing (runCase/previewLines) only to the new section-7b MUST_DIFFER/MUST_COLLAPSE matrix, which covers the CHK-001-vs-CHK-002 half (case checklist-ordinal, prints both strings literally) but NOT the free-standing-counter half: that claim is grounded in the pre-existing section-7 assertion at lines 166-175 (gate BLOCKED for B-bbaf at ...(attempt 3) vs ...(attempt 41)), which has no console.log at all — verified by running node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js and grepping the full output for the word attempt: zero matches. The only trace in the printed output is the terse final-summary fragment gate-repeat digest/reset, which states neither attempt, free-standing counter, nor digest identically. So CHK-003 second half is still exactly the F-008 defect (userSees describes a passing check whose content is not literally on screen) that the round-2 fix was supposed to close story-wide; it closed CHK-001/CHK-002/CHK-003-first-half but left this one clause unaddressed.

packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:280-284 — the leaseNonOwner fixture (labelled by the surrounding comment at line 273-279 as Real production rejection messages ... Reproduced from their build sites, not invented) renders the ownership class as the literal word mutating: an owner-gated mutating command. The real formatNonOwnerError (core/story-owner-lease.ts:637) interpolates ctx.ownershipClass verbatim, and story_advance actual ownershipClass per core/command-policy.ts:152 is storyScopedMutating, one of exactly five valid OwnershipClass enum values (readOnly/storyScopedMutating/reviewerWrite/mainSharedMutating/dangerousMutating per core/command-policy.ts:66-71) — mutating is not a member of that enum and never appears in a real rendered message. This does not affect the digest assertion under test (guardedBy duration-rule only exercises the heartbeat-age token), so the case still validly proves what it claims, but it is a factual deviation from the real string this fixture is presented as reproducing verbatim, and could mislead a future reader into believing mutating is a real ownershipClass value. Fix: use storyScopedMutating to match the real rendered text exactly.

checklist.json:74-83 CHK-001:edge:0 verificationEvidence still cites the weak Case 'sanity-bound' shape-check (smoke.ts:603-606, assert.match(...,/^story_advance\/[0-9a-f]{12}$/)) as proof the retained sanity bound 'is exercised rather than silently absent' -- this is the exact F-001 defect recurring at the same intent id after the fix. The F-001 fix added the real load-bearing proof as matrix case 'sanity-bound-is-applied' (smoke.ts:446-458, guardedBy sanity-bound), but the evidence record attached to CHK-001:edge:0 was never updated to cite it. Verified empirically: removed .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) from boundReasonForDigest (convergence-breaker.ts:497), rebuilt, reran the smoke -- the cited shape-check still PASSED unchanged (a well-formed digest exists regardless of the bound), while sanity-bound-is-applied and beyond-sanity-bound failed exactly as designed (localization: sanity-bound -> beyond-sanity-bound, sanity-bound-is-applied; all other 18 cases still passed). So CHK-001:edge:0 currently has zero evidence proving its own claimed property; the real proof exists in the code but is filed under CHK-001:edge:1 instead.

All 19 verificationEvidence entries in checklist.json were recorded 2026-07-24T00:20:24-00:20:43Z (commits 15a8200c52..f1784aecf9), ~70min BEFORE the round-1 fix commit 08bd949d5a (01:30:25Z) that substantially rewrote convergence-breaker-smoke.ts in response to F-001..F-009, and none were refreshed afterward (no verification_evidence_add commits after f1784aecf9). Reproduced concrete stale citations against current code: (1) checklist.json:182 CHK-002:edge:0 and :274 CHK-003:edge:0 cite guard tag [guard: collapse-lane] -- no longer exists (current GuardRule union = truncation-removal|sanity-bound|path-rule|windows-path-rule|duration-rule|digit-rule|hex-rule, smoke.ts:300-307). (2) checklist.json:274-283 CHK-003:edge:0 cites case must-still-collapse timestamp-and-attempt-counter -- no case by that name exists anywhere in MUST_DIFFER/MUST_COLLAPSE (grep confirms zero matches); CHK-003:edge:0s intent (timestamp+counter collapse) has no evidence citing an actually-existing case. (3) checklist.json:98,206,298 (CHK-001/002/003:adversarial:0) report totals (N of 12); current matrix totals 20 cases (8 must-differ+12 must-still-collapse, smoke.ts:827). (4) checklist.json:298 CHK-003:adversarial:0 and :403 CHK-004:adversarial:0 claim restoring the unconditional digit-run rewrite fails exactly digit-rule -> checklist-ordinal, review-round-ordinal, story-id (3 cases). Reproduced this revert against current code (build+run): it now fails FOUR cases -- the three named plus dotted-version-requirement, added since this evidence was recorded to guard F-002s v0.3.229-vs-v0.3.230 fix. The evidence own localization claim is now factually wrong against the code it evidences. (5) checklist.json:356 CHK-004:happy:0 says All 7 must-differ cases -- current count is 8; checklist.json:379 CHK-004:edge:0 says All 5 must-still-collapse cases -- current count is 12. (6) none of the 19 entries cite by name any of lease-non-owner-heartbeat-age, active-lease-takeover-refusal, main-write-lock-contention, validation-lock-contention (the 4 duration-rule production-message cases), windows-absolute-path, delimiter-attached-absolute-path, machine-path-into-repo-relative-segments, hex-id, dotted-version-requirement, or sanity-bound-is-applied -- every case added or materially changed by the fix commit has zero evidence naming it, even though CHK-002:edge:1s intent (normalized once, no partially-rewritten remainder) is only actually proven by machine-path-into-repo-relative-segments/delimiter-attached-absolute-path, neither ever cited.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:538 the pre-existing hex-id rule /\b[0-9a-f]{7,}\b/g runs BEFORE the CHK-003 number rule (:581) and has no identifier-attachment protection (only a bare \b word-boundary, not the [\w.-] lookbehind/lookahead the number rule uses). Since decimal digits 0-9 are a subset of hex digits 0-9a-f, ANY identifier-attached decimal digit run of 7+ characters is consumed by this earlier rule before the number rule ever sees it, so CHK-003s documented contract (checklist.json CHK-003:edge:1: a story id whose digits are attached to an identifier survives normalization; JSDoc :523-526) silently fails once the digit run reaches 7 characters. Verified against the built module: gateFailureDigest(cmd,gate BLOCKED: session-1234567 failed) === gateFailureDigest(cmd,gate BLOCKED: session-7654321 failed) COLLAPSE, and worker-1721775600 vs worker-1721775601 (epoch-suffixed ids) also COLLAPSE -- while the identical construction with a 6-digit suffix (session-123456 vs session-654321) correctly stays DISTINCT, proving the 7-digit hex-rule threshold is exactly what breaks the promise. This is an over-collapse: two DIFFERENT identifiers (e.g. two different epoch-timestamp-suffixed session/worker ids, or any numeric identifier reaching 7 digits) read as one gate failing twice -- precisely the false-freeze failure mode this story exists to eliminate -- and it is not covered by any MUST_DIFFER matrix case (checklist-ordinal/review-round-ordinal/story-id/dotted-version-requirement all use digit runs under 7 characters, so the matrix never exercises this rule-ordering interaction).

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:568 and :581 -- the widened [\w.-] protection set added by this round (F-002/F-007) makes the duration rules and the number rules trailing lookahead (?![\w.-]) treat a literal sentence-ending period (no preceding space) as a protected identifier character, so a standalone counter or duration immediately followed by . fails to normalize. Verified against the built module: gateFailureDigest(cmd,Retry count exceeded 5.) !== gateFailureDigest(cmd,Retry count exceeded 19.) (DISTINCT -- should collapse, both are free-standing counters differing only in incidental value) and the same holds for the duration rule (heartbeat 45s. vs heartbeat 46s. stay DISTINCT while heartbeat 45s  vs heartbeat 46s  with a trailing space correctly COLLAPSE). This contradicts the functions own documented contract (:521-526, STANDALONE numbers only... -> #, with no punctuation caveat) and CHK-003s edge-case intent (free-standing counters... still produce one digest key, so genuine retries of one failure keep accumulating). It reintroduces the same under-collapse class that F-007 fixed for units (a livelock that never accumulates because every retry mints a fresh key), for any rejection message that happens to end a bare number/duration right before a period with no separating space -- a common English sentence-final construction. Not covered by the smoke matrix: the closest fixture (negative-counter, MUST_COLLAPSE) uses -5 remaining before the gate refuses (trailing space), never a trailing period.
findings.resolvedReason: Split by the round-4 policy, so recorded as partially mitigated rather than fixed or superseded. DURATION HALF — RETAINED AND STILL FIXED: heartbeat 45s. and 46s. collapse, the duration rule keeps its (?<!\d\.) and (?!\.\d) lookarounds, and must-still-collapse case sentence-final-duration guards it; this half has a real producer, formatLeaseAge. NUMBER HALF — SUPERSEDED: exceeded 5. and exceeded 19. no longer collapse, because honouring that requires the general free-standing-number rule that collapsed the F-020 shapes, and no producer emits a bare sentence-final ordinal into a gate rejection. The fixture is converted to must-differ case sentence-final-counter-now-distinct rather than deleted, so the re-decision is visible in the matrix. Consequence recorded honestly in plan.md section 5: the RED harness tmp/s3-red/red-s3-digest-collapse.mjs now reports 7/8 exit 1, because its K1 assertion bundles an ISO-timestamp claim (still true) with an attempt-counter claim (re-decided). K1 was NOT edited to pass; a comment above it explains why, and both halves are re-asserted separately and correctly in the smoke as iso-timestamp-only and attempt-counter-now-distinct. All five defect classes C1a, C1b, C2, C3 and C4 pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:556 vs :588/:612 — the round-3 F-014 fix gave the hex rule identifier-attachment lookarounds (?<![\w-])...(?![\w-]) but NOT the dot-adjacency lookarounds (?<!\d\.)/(?!\.\d) that the round-3 F-015 fix gave the duration rule (:588) and number rule (:612). Since the hex rule runs first and decimal digits are a subset of hex digits, a FREE-STANDING (non-identifier-attached) decimal number or duration whose integer part is >=7 digits gets its integer part eaten by the hex rule alone, before the duration/number rule ever sees the full digits+fraction (or digits+unit) shape as one token — splitting one logical value into two # tokens instead of one. This makes the normalized SHAPE depend on whether the integer part crosses the hex rule's 7-digit threshold, so two otherwise-identical incidental-noise messages straddling that boundary fail to collapse into the same digest. Verified empirically against the freshly rebuilt dist (packages/main/dist/core/convergence-breaker.js) at HEAD 68f2fabbe9 (round-3 commit ba2ac008e5): gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 123456.5ms ago") !== gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 1234567.5ms ago") (DISTINCT — both are pure wall-clock noise per the duration rule's own stated purpose and should collapse), while gateFailureDigest of two 7+-digit fractional durations against EACH OTHER, and two <7-digit fractional durations against EACH OTHER, both correctly COLLAPSE — isolating the defect to exactly the digit-count-crossing case. Same effect on the plain number rule: "attempt 41.5 failed" vs "attempt 1234567.5 failed" is DISTINCT. This is the identical failure class F-007/F-015 were filed to fix (a genuine retry sequence silently mints a fresh key and the repeat counter never reaches 2, so assessBreaker never trips gate-repeat for that pair) but for the newly-introduced hex/duration-number lookaround asymmetry, and none of the 24 CHK-004 matrix cases exercise a free-standing decimal with a >=7-digit integer part (the only hex-adjacent must-differ case, identifier-attached-long-decimal, is hyphen-attached with no fractional dot). Fix: give the hex rule the same (?<!\d\.)/(?!\.\d) lookarounds as the duration/number rules, or otherwise ensure it does not consume a digit run immediately followed by .digit.
findings.resolvedReason: The free-standing hash rule now carries the dot-adjacency lookarounds it was missing: (?<![\w-])(?<!\d\.)[0-9a-f]{7,}(?![\w-])(?!\.\d). The reported pair now collapses — verified with the exact reproduction from the finding, gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 123456.5ms ago") === gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 1234567.5ms ago") — and is guarded as must-still-collapse matrix case decimal-duration-straddling-hash-threshold, tagged hex-dot-adjacency. Revert-proved: removing (?!\.\d) alone fails that case and NO other, so the tag localizes exactly. The finding also reported the same asymmetry on the plain number rule ("attempt 41.5 failed" vs "attempt 1234567.5 failed"); that rule no longer exists — the general free-standing-number rule was deleted in the round-4 policy convergence (see F-020), so that half of the report is resolved by removal rather than by a lookaround. (?<!\d\.) is retained as the symmetric half; it has no named producer and the source comment says so rather than implying one.

findings.desc: CHK-004:edge:0 and CHK-004:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence (checklist.json) claim the 24-case matrix and its nine revert-proofs comprehensively guard the must-still-collapse direction ('proving the breaker keeps catching a genuine repeat'; 'each leaving all other cases passing'), but this is not true against the exact code at the current HEAD: B-bf52:F-016 (open, unresolved, filed by lattice-review-quality at RR-014 against the same head 68f2fabbe9/material 141ee128..., code unchanged since) shows the hex rule (convergence-breaker.ts:556) lacks the (?<!\d\.)/(?!\.\d) dot-adjacency lookarounds that the duration rule (:588) and number rule (:612) both carry, so a free-standing decimal or duration whose integer part is >=7 digits gets split across the hex and duration/number rules and fails to collapse. Independently reproduced against packages/main/dist/core/convergence-breaker.js: gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 123456.5ms ago") !== gateFailureDigest("story_advance","heartbeat 1234567.5ms ago") (both pure wall-clock noise, must collapse per the duration rule's own stated purpose, but do not), and gateFailureDigest("story_advance","attempt 41.5 failed") !== gateFailureDigest("story_advance","attempt 1234567.5 failed") (same asymmetry on the plain number rule). None of the 24 matrix cases in convergence-breaker-smoke.ts exercise a free-standing decimal/duration with a >=7-digit integer part (the only hex-adjacent must-differ case, identifier-attached-long-decimal, is hyphen-attached, not free-standing), so the gap is real and untested. This is the same under-collapse failure class (a genuine retry mints a fresh key and gate-repeat never reaches 2, so assessBreaker never trips) that F-007/F-015 were filed to fix, now open a third time under F-016 for the newly-introduced hex/duration-number lookaround asymmetry. Until F-016 is fixed AND a matrix case is added to guard it, CHK-004's completeness claim in its own verificationEvidence is overstated, and the round-3 re-recording (all 19 entries otherwise verified accurate and reproducible against the current code) is not yet safe to pass on the coverage dimension.
findings.resolvedReason: The underlying gap F-017 depends on (F-016) is fixed and is now exercised: must-still-collapse case decimal-duration-straddling-hash-threshold covers a free-standing decimal whose integer part crosses the 7-character threshold, which no case previously did. The matrix is no longer the 24 cases and 9 revert-proofs this finding assessed: it is 15 must-differ plus 15 must-still-collapse, and 14 surgical reverts were executed against the built smoke, each failing exactly its tagged subset. CHK-004 verificationEvidence must be re-recorded to those numbers before this resolution is complete; that is a main-agent write and is deliberately not performed from the implementer lane.

findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:0 verificationEvidence (checklist.json) states the two reconstructed DEV-gate renders are 'identical for the first 244 normalized characters and differing only in the outstanding gap', repeating a figure that also appears in plan.md sec 1/3 and convergence-breaker.ts:469-470. Verified this number against the actual code: reconstructing the exact devGateRejection('B-d877', [...]) fixture used by the case (smoke.ts:263-277) and running it through gateFailureDigest's own normalization, the shared FIXED HEADER (preamble + diagnostics/mode/status/blocking/hardening/ledger lines, before the gap list) normalizes to 328 chars without the preamble or 423 chars with it -- not 244 under either reading. The smoke's own printed preview for this exact case (dev-gate-one-gap-differs) reports the compared values 'share their first 617 chars' before diverging, since case a/b also share their entire first gap (GAP_SNAPSHOT). This is a low-severity factual inaccuracy, not a coverage gap: the underlying case is genuine (verified by direct reproduction -- restoring the pre-story 200-char cut fails exactly {dev-gate-one-gap-differs, dev-gate-gap-count-differs} and no other case), and the qualitative point (the real header exceeds the old 200-char truncation) holds even more strongly than the 244 figure implies. But the number was seemingly never recomputed against the current renderProofStoryDiagnosticReport (which already included the Hardening/Ledger lines, added 2026-06-29/30, well before this story's branch) at any of the three places it was copied -- plan.md, the source comment, and now the round-3 evidence note -- an unverified figure restated three times rather than measured once.
findings.resolvedReason: The 244 figure is retracted in all three places it was copied (plan.md section 1, the convergence-breaker.ts source comment, and this storys own prose) and replaced with MEASURED values, stated as measured: 257 normalized characters for the machine.ts preamble plus the reports six header lines, and 433 by the point the first gap row begins in a two-trigger report. Root cause found while measuring, and fixed: the smoke fixture rendered the ledger thresholdState as (within), but the real union at core/types.ts:2529 is within_threshold | too_broad | slice_required, so (within) is not a value this code can emit. That abbreviation is exactly the 10 characters by which every earlier count was short — it is why this finding measured 423 where the real render gives 433. The fixture now renders (within_threshold). The substantive claim is unchanged and holds with room to spare: the former 200-character cut landed inside the fixed header, before any gap row.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 3), recorded by the main agent because codex-cli is not a registered dispatch actor: a THIRD inverse-risk instance. The review-run-binding rejection rendered via evaluateReviewVerdict/getGuardFailureReason interpolates a run id, e.g. "finding F-abc bound reviewRunId B-bf52:RR-001: Not the latest run on the current lane (current: B-bf52:RR-002)" then "(current: B-bf52:RR-003)". The digits are identifier-attached so the number rule preserves them; a host that starts a new reviewer run between attempts at the same blocked transition mints a new counter key every time and maxGateRepeat never reaches 2. NOT refuted by reset semantics: cli-engine.ts:1405 resets only on a SUCCESSFUL story_advance, deliberately scoped so a trivial mutation cannot clear the counter.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed real and accepted as a residual, recorded in plan.md section 4.3 rather than fixed. RR-002 and RR-003 do keep separate keys, so a host that starts a new reviewer run between attempts never accumulates a gate-repeat count for that rejection. It is not fixable in the direction this story must fail: an identifier-attached PURE-DECIMAL suffix is syntactically indistinguishable from CHK-002, so any rule that collapses RR-002 also collapses CHK-002 and reintroduces the false freeze this story exists to remove. The findings observation that the counter reset does not mitigate it is CONFIRMED, not disputed: cli-engine.ts:1405 resets only on a SUCCESSFUL story_advance, deliberately scoped so a trivial mutation cannot clear the counter. The un-caught runaway is bounded by the burn-alert system, which watches spend rather than message text; the false freeze it replaces is bounded only by an interactive human TTY acknowledgement.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 3), recorded by the main agent: removing the dot from the protection classes made the general bare-number rule collapse SUBSTANTIVELY different values in a REAL reachable message. test-evidence output is interpolated verbatim into a story_advance DONE rejection at machine.ts:1190, so "test FAIL: connection to localhost:3000 refused" and the same with :4000 digest identically, as do coverage 24% versus 25% and ratio 0.75 versus 0.80. Two DIFFERENT validation failures therefore read as one gate failing twice and falsely freeze the story: the exact defect class this story exists to remove, reintroduced by its own fix.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by deleting the general free-standing-number rule outright rather than by adding another lookaround. This finding is what decided the round-4 policy: rounds 1-3 oscillated because a bare number is not syntactically decidable as substantive or volatile, so every narrowing produced a never-trips case and every widening produced a false-freeze case. The tie was broken on producers — (attempt N), the shape the number rule existed to absorb, has no producer anywhere in this repo outside the smokes own fixture, while this findings shapes are real and reachable through the verbatim test-evidence interpolation at machine.ts. All three reported pairs now keep separate keys and are guarded as must-differ cases test-output-port, test-output-percentage and test-output-decimal-threshold, built from the real Cannot enter DONE: test FAIL: <output> rendering and tagged number-rule-removal. Revert-proved: reintroducing the number rule in EITHER the narrow round-1..3 form or the unconditional pre-story form fails all three.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 3), recorded by the main agent: matrix case identifier-attached-long-decimal is tagged solely hex-rule-overreach but also depends on the number rule staying narrow. Restoring the former unconditional digit rewrite makes it fail alongside the four correctly-tagged digit-rule-overreach cases, so the matrix invariant that guardedBy names the rule whose mutation makes a case fail is untrue for this case and can send a maintainer to the wrong rule.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved and independently verified. The dual dependence this finding reported disappeared with the number rule: with that rule deleted, identifier-attached-long-decimal still passes, so the dependence was never load-bearing. The case is retagged from hex-rule-overreach to attached-hash-overreach, which is now the tightest available name for it — dropping the new attached-hash rules a-f LETTER requirement collapses worker-1721775600 and fails THIS CASE AND NOTHING ELSE, revert-proved against the built smoke. The residual same-direction overlap is stated in the case comment rather than hidden: it fails equally if the free-standing hash rules (?<![\w-]) anchor is dropped, and reintroducing the unconditional /\d+/g fails it alongside the four digit-rule-overreach cases, which is the same-direction overlap the matrix header already documents as acceptable.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts gateFailureDigest still silently disarms the breaker for a THIRD real story_advance-reachable producer: the ownership-gate rejection embeds the BLOCKED (current) session id via formatNonOwnerError (core/story-owner-lease.ts:636-638 "so this session (${ctx.currentSessionId}) cannot run it"), fed by cli/ownership-gate.ts:317 currentSessionId: getSessionId(). Whenever LATTICE_SESSION_ID and every supported host-adapter env var (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CODEX_*, ANTIGRAVITY_*, ...) are absent, owner-session.ts:28-32 deriveLocalSessionId falls back to sessionSource=derived-ppid and mints sess-${sha256(host,root,ppid).slice(0,16)} -- a value that changes on EVERY fresh CLI invocation because process.ppid differs per process (this is the code's own documented degraded path: owner-session.ts:83 warns "session identity degraded: derived-ppid; export LATTICE_SESSION_ID ... before repeated mutating commands"). Verified empirically: two separate node invocations in this worktree with no session env vars set produced ppid 8629 -> sess-d7efe197b316c43a and ppid 16456 -> sess-f278b84bbcb06149. Because this 16-hex-char suffix is attached to "sess" by a HYPHEN, convergence-breaker.ts's hex rule (:556), duration rule (:588) and number rule (:612) all treat it as a protected identifier (their shared (?<![\w-]) lookbehind excludes hyphen-attached runs) and never normalize it -- correct for a STABLE identifier like a story id, wrong here because this specific suffix is per-process noise, not identity. Reproduced end-to-end against the built dist with the real functions (deriveLocalSessionId + formatNonOwnerError + gateFailureDigest): two renderings of the identical real ownership-gate rejection (same foreign owner B-bf52 lease, same command, differing only in the blocked session's derived-ppid suffix) hash to story_advance/6bad05ab768c vs story_advance/48de9a1498fe -- they do NOT collapse. Consequence: an agent or human retrying story_advance against a live foreign lease with no session-id env configured (plain terminal, CI script, or any unsupported host harness -- the exact same class of caller the derived-ppid warning already flags) mints a brand-new gate-failure-counts.json key on every single retry; maxGateFailureCount never reaches 2 and the convergence breaker never trips for this genuinely repeating rejection -- the same silent-non-firing failure mode as F-007/F-014, via a different real producer this round's fix did not cover. Fix direction: normalize the derived-ppid sess-<hex> suffix specifically (e.g. treat a hyphen-attached hex run of 12+ chars immediately following the literal token "sess-" as volatile), or have formatNonOwnerError omit/shorten the untrusted local session id from the message text used for counting, without touching the CHK-002/CHK-003 identifier-preservation guarantees for real identifiers like story ids and checklist ids.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed with a new attached-hash rule at position 2 of the chain: (?<=[-_])(?=[0-9a-f]*[a-f])[0-9a-f]{7,}(?![\w-]) -> #. A hyphen or underscore attached run of 7+ hex characters CONTAINING AT LEAST ONE a-f LETTER is provably a digest and never a human ordinal, so sess-d7efe197b316c43a collapses while session-1234567 and worker-1721775600 stay distinct — the letter requirement is what satisfies this finding without reopening F-014, and it is the one place where a SHAPE cleanly separates the two directions a bare number cannot. Chosen over the findings alternative of special-casing the literal sess- token because it is structural rather than an enumeration. Guarded by must-still-collapse case ppid-derived-session-id, which CALLS the real deriveLocalSessionId and the real formatNonOwnerError rendering rather than imitating them, varies only the PPID, and asserts both generated digests actually contain an a-f letter so the fixture cannot silently degenerate into one that passes for the wrong reason. Revert-proved: deleting the rule fails that case and no other.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 4), recorded by the main agent: the ppid-derived-session-id fixture varies the LEASE OWNER session id while claiming to model one retrying host. formatNonOwnerError (story-owner-lease.ts:636) renders lease.sessionId as the owner and ctx.currentSessionId as the rejected caller; a genuine retry against the same owner keeps lease.sessionId CONSTANT, and a change to it means ownership actually changed, i.e. a substantively different failure. The attached-hash rule collapses them anyway, so an owner change between two rejected attempts now falsely freezes the story. The smoke therefore guards the opposite of the required behavior. Same token shape, opposite requirement by position: the attached-hash rule cannot distinguish them.

cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 4), recorded by the main agent: the attached-hash rule requires an a-f letter to prove a run is a digest, which leaves an unbounded retry hole for all-decimal digest prefixes. codex brute-forced deriveLocalSessionId over ppid values and found real examples sess-0378592327422727 and sess-1686256634242425 whose rejection renderings produce DISTINCT keys. Probability (10/16)^16, about 1 in 2815 derived sessions, so not merely theoretical: such a caller can evade accumulation indefinitely.

cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 4), recorded by the main agent: plan.md justifies accepting under-normalization by claiming the residual runaway risk is bounded by this repo burn-alert system. That claim is FALSE. Burn scanning runs only through doctor and usage_sweep (handlers/doctor.ts:146, core/usage-burn-alert.ts:348), labels itself advisory, supplies no gate evidence, never changes exit status, cannot stop a session, and is disabled by LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0. The accepted residuals therefore have NO automatic bound inside a story_advance retry loop, and the justification must be corrected rather than restated.

Round-4's central premise ("(attempt N) has NO producer anywhere in this repo... exists only as the smoke's own invented fixture", convergence-breaker.ts:530-536,661-662 and plan.md sec 2.2) was validated only against this branch's own stale merge-base, not against current main. This worktree branched 98 commits before B-cc54 (commits d07885e8c8..7db9b3bd1d, merged bdca6ae59c) landed on main, which ALREADY fixed the identical C1 defect class (200-char truncation collapsing different ProofStory DEV-gate rejections) via a different mechanism: extractGateBlockSignals (main repo convergence-breaker.ts:504-541) folds structurally-extracted bracketed/snake_case gap-id signals into the hash basis alongside the still-truncated 200-char prefix. B-cc54's OWN dedicated regression suite, packages/main/src/tasks/gate-repeat-block-smoke.ts (main repo, NOT present in this branch, wired as a doneRequiredCommand at lattice.config.json:95 validate.commands), asserts at CHK-001:adversarial:0 (lines 151-155) that GATE-blocked-at-path-ISO-id-hex-attempt-7 and the same string with attempt-91 MUST digest identically (comment: volatile-token noise must still collapse) -- i.e. main's already-DONE, already-shipped behavior treats a bare attempt-counter as noise that collapses, directly contradicting round-4's premise that this shape has no real stakeholder. VERIFIED by direct reproduction: copied gate-repeat-block-smoke.ts into this worktree, built cleanly (no compile errors -- extractGateBlockSignals is not imported elsewhere), and ran it against this story's round-4 gateFailureDigest -- it CRASHES with an uncaught AssertionError at CHK-001:adversarial:0 (actual story_advance/3e5b2a23a3d9 vs expected story_advance/51cd2e515802), reproduced twice under verified clean-tree conditions. Separately, running tmp/s3-red/red-s3-digest-collapse.mjs against the CURRENT main repo dist (proofbound/packages/main/dist, the true pre-merge baseline, not this branch stale merge-base) gives 4/9 FAIL (C2,C3,C4,K1b), not the 6/9 the story baseline narrative assumes, because B-cc54 signal extraction already independently fixes the C1a/C1b cases this story also targets. Consequence: this branch cannot cleanly merge into main (git 3-way merge on convergence-breaker.ts conflicts, both sides rewrote the same function region), and whichever resolution is chosen must reconcile with B-cc54's shipped, doneRequiredCommand-gated regression suite -- a reconciliation never evaluated across any of the 4 review rounds; background.md and plan.md never mention B-cc54. This is not a request to keep the deleted bare-number rule; the story's deciding evidence (no real producer) is empirically false once measured against current main, and merging as-is breaks an existing passing DONE-gate test.

checklist.json CHK-003 userSees (frozen field) says: the convergence-breaker smoke prints a passing check that two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still digest identically. The delivered behavior is the OPPOSITE: convergence-breaker.ts:573-668 deletes the general free-standing-number rule, and the matrix case attempt-counter-now-distinct (convergence-breaker-smoke.ts) asserts two such attempts now digest DIFFERENTLY. This is a genuine userSees-vs-code mismatch, not merely a stale description of an unrelated detail -- a reader who trusts CHK-003.userSees literally, without independently cross-referencing plan.md sec 4.2 or the CHK-003:edge:0 verificationEvidence note, will believe the opposite of what ships. The implementer's handling is honest (the verificationEvidence note for CHK-003:edge:0 is explicitly headed HONEST DIVERGENCE FROM THE FROZEN userSees and plan.md sec 4.2 + its closing paragraph both flag the drift and correctly note that editing checklist metadata is outside an implementer's write scope) but not sufficient on its own: the userSees field itself, which is the canonical user-facing contract other readers/gates trust, remains false. Recommend: whoever owns checklist metadata updates CHK-003.title/userSees to describe the round-4 delivered behavior (attempt-style bare counters now stay distinct; only provably-volatile shapes collapse) rather than leaving the frozen field asserting the reverted round-1..3 behavior.

recorded by the main agent on behalf of the test-coverage lane, whose prompt envelope was invalidated mid-review by the concurrent main merge: CHK-004:adversarial:0 evidence claims fourteen revert-proofs across TEN guard groups. The fourteen is correct and the lane reproduced every one exactly, but the group count is wrong: thirteen distinct guardedBy tags are actually used across the 30 cases, and the smoke file own comment block clusters them into seven named categories, so no grouping yields ten. Same defect class as F-013 item 4 and F-017: a specific checkable numeric claim in verificationEvidence that does not hold. Note this evidence note is being rewritten anyway by the B-cc54 reconciliation, which replaces the matrix.

cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 5), recorded by the main agent: the substantive-id allowlist omits BUG-. Real producer at packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:1195 renders "Cannot enter DONE: 1 unfixed bug(s): BUG-001"; that and the BUG-002 variant both digest to story_advance/a3e4d0356493. Fixing BUG-001 and then being blocked by BUG-002 is substantive progress read as one repeated failure, i.e. the exact false freeze this story exists to remove. Proves the hand-written enumeration is incomplete and needs a completeness guard, not just one more entry.
findings.resolvedReason: bug- added to SUBSTANTIVE_ID_PREFIXES so BUG-001/BUG-002 (machine.ts:1195) key distinctly. Added completeness guard convergence-breaker-smoke.ts section 7c: comment-aware scan of core/handlers id-mint (PREFIX-\${) and rejection-literal ordinal shapes; every discovered prefix must be allowlisted or in an explicit commented exclusion category, else it fails naming the offending prefix. Verified: BUG-001/BUG-002 distinct; revert-proof removing bug- fails only unfixed-bug-ordinal (1/18); dropping tea- from exclusions fails the completeness guard naming tea-.

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 5), recorded by the main agent: putting RR- in the allowlist knowingly reintroduces the inverse-risk hole codex filed in round 3. "Cannot enter TEST: review pass RP-001 bound reviewRunId B-bf52:RR-002 is stale" and the RR-003 variant now digest differently, and starting another reviewer run does NOT repair stale evidence, so a host repeating review_run_start then story_advance mints a fresh key indefinitely and the breaker never trips. Worse, the matrix case review-run-ordinal asserts that unsafe behaviour AS DESIRED. RR- and RP- name review bookkeeping that changes on retry, not the artifact that must be fixed, so they do not belong in an allowlist whose stated criterion is naming WHICH artifact failed.
findings.resolvedReason: rr-/rp- removed from SUBSTANTIVE_ID_PREFIXES in core/convergence-breaker.ts; review bookkeeping changes on retry and does not name the artifact to fix, and starting another reviewer run does not repair stale evidence. The unsafe must-differ review-run-ordinal case is replaced by a must-collapse stale-review-run-evidence case (guard review-bookkeeping-not-allowlisted) whose comment records it previously asserted the unsafe direction. Verified: RR-002/RR-003 stale renderings collapse; revert-proof re-adding rr-/rp- fails only that case (1/18).

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 5), recorded by the main agent: CHK-001 carries status done with result pass while its evidence states NOT DELIVERED BY THIS STORY. That is internally contradictory, and if B-cc54 structural-signal mechanism regressed this story would contain no independent implementation satisfying the item. Main agent follow-up: removing the truncation outright does break B-cc54 suite (measured, exit 1), but a signals-conditional prefix does not, and delivers the item honestly.
findings.resolvedReason: CHK-001 delivered: gateFailureDigest prefix cut is now signals-conditional (signals present -> slice(0,200), B-cc54 preserved exactly; signal-less -> slice(0,16384) sanity bound) so a late-diverging signal-less scope-gate rejection keeps a distinct key. Removing the truncation outright breaks B-cc54 (measured exit 1); the conditional does not. Added must-differ signal-less-long-rejection (guard signals-conditional-prefix) and red-s3 C1c, plus the test-coverage-lane signals-fold case proofstory-gap-signal-set (guard signals-fold) that genuinely exercises B-cc54 C1. Verified: gate-repeat-block-smoke exit 0 with zero diff vs main, convergence-breaker-smoke exit 0, red-s3 9/9; revert-proofs isolate each case (1/18).

findings.desc: cross-host (codex-cli host-B round 6), recorded by the main agent: sep- is a REAL substantive artifact-id prefix wrongly placed in the completeness guard exclusion list at convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:871. Producer scope-anti-expansion.ts:120 mints SEP-<storyId>-<NNN>; machine.ts:269 renders them into a story_advance INIT_CHECK rejection. SEP-B-bf52-001 and SEP-B-bf52-002 collapse to story_advance/e2db55c93f47, so a host resolving scope-extension proposals sequentially falsely freezes. This is an F-029-class hole hidden inside the guard: the scan DOES discover sep-, but the false exclusion makes it report all-classified. TWO fixes required: (1) remove sep- from the exclusion list and make it substantive; (2) SEP is a COMPOUND id SEP-<storyId>-<ordinal> where only the final ordinal is substantive and the storyId in the middle is constant within a per-story counter, so the allowlist mechanism (which only inspects the single prefix immediately before a digit run) cannot protect the trailing ordinal by adding sep- alone; the digit rule must recognise a substantive artifact id as a WHOLE token (an allowlisted prefix followed by the rest of its id ending in a digit) and protect it entire. Main agent validated a whole-token approach 17/17 including SEP-001 vs SEP-002 distinct while b-1234/b-5678, story ids, attempts, heartbeats and RR- all still collapse.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:673 — the signals-conditional 200-char prefix cut is NOT relaxed when two rejections have an IDENTICAL, non-empty signal set but differ only in an embedded allowlisted ordinal past char 200. extractGateBlockSignals only captures the gap CODE (e.g. milestone_source_requirement_unbound, acceptance_binding_unknown_checklist_ref), never the specific object the gap names, so two genuinely different ProofStory DEV-gate rejections collapse. Repro with 100% real production code (core/proofstory.ts renderProofStoryDiagnosticReport + the exact machine.ts:179 banner + bumpGateFailureCount): a milestone-ledger gap naming sourceRequirementId REQ-001 vs the SAME gap code naming REQ-002 on a different milestone digest IDENTICALLY (story_advance/b5117552c0ff both times) even though REQ- is allowlisted and the strings genuinely diverge at char 450 (past the 200-char cut). Same mechanism reproduced with acceptance_binding_unknown_checklist_ref naming CHK-005 vs CHK-006 (also identical digest, story_advance/011867525d4e both times) — so this is a GENERAL flaw affecting any/all of the 7 allowlisted prefixes when they appear inside a ProofStory diagnostic-gap message, not one specific prefix. Confirmed end-to-end: two bumpGateFailureCount calls with these real REQ-001/REQ-002 renders leave maxGateFailureCount=2, the exact breaker-trip threshold — a false freeze on a story making incremental progress (fix REQ-001, then get correctly blocked by the separate, later-discovered REQ-002 gap), which is precisely the class of bug CHK-001 exists to close. tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts signals-fold/proofstory-gap-signal-set case only tests DIFFERENT gap codes (assert.notDeepEqual(sigA, sigB) at line ~412) and never tests the SAME gap code recurring with a different embedded ordinal, so this gap is untested. Fix direction: extractGateBlockSignals must also capture the substantive ordinal(s) embedded inside each gap message (not just the code), or the signals-branch prefix must not be capped at 200 when the message contains an allowlisted-prefix ordinal beyond that cut.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:594 - the allowlisted prefix `init-` protects the wrong id shape: it is dead for the real story_advance-gated INIT_CHECK rejection and does not protect the id convention that rejection actually uses. The only literal `INIT-${...}` mint site in the repo is handlers/draft-check.ts:81, which feeds `story_create --fromDraft` (handlers/story-create.ts GATE 3 draft_check_blocking_issues, ~line 636), and cli-engine.ts:1508 only calls bumpGateFailureCount `if (cmd === 'story_advance')` - a story_create failure NEVER reaches the breaker, so this mint site can never collide or protect anything. Meanwhile the REAL INIT_CHECK gate reachable via story_advance is core/machine.ts:1036-1039 (`Cannot enter INIT_CHECK: init-check reviewer recorded high/critical issues...` embedding `${issue.id}`), sourced from `init_check_set` issues - and the AUTHORITATIVE schema at cli/command-catalog.ts:2315 documents the convention verbatim: `id: z.string().optional().describe('Reviewer self-assigned ID, for example I-1; optional.')`. Prefix `i-`, not `init-`, and `i-` is absent from SUBSTANTIVE_ID_PREFIXES. Repro with the real machine.ts:1036 banner and the real reviewer agentId `lattice-review-story-init` (the primary INIT reviewer per templates/agents/lattice-review-story-init.md): two GENUINELY DIFFERENT high/critical init-check issues, id=I-1 then id=I-2 (reviewer flags I-1, main agent fixes it, reviewer re-runs and flags a new, different critical problem I-2) digest IDENTICALLY (story_advance/a5649c7798c7 both times) because `i-` normalizes to `i-#`. bumpGateFailureCount confirms maxGateFailureCount=2 after these two calls - the breaker-trip threshold, a false freeze exactly like the fixed BUG-/F-030 case. This also exposes a structural blind spot in the section-7c completeness guard: it can only discover prefixes that appear as LITERAL text in source (template mint `PREFIX-${` or a literal `PREFIX-\d` inside a rejection-marked string); a reviewer-free-text id that reaches a rejection only via runtime `${issue.id}` interpolation is invisible to it, so `all classified` from that guard does not mean the allowlist is actually complete for this class of producer.
